findings.detail: Frequency deciles are assigned by item rank, splitting equal-frequency items across deciles. Thus items with identical training frequency can receive different repeat-propensity/purchase-rate quantile populations and consequently different suffixes, depending on item ordering. This does not faithfully define bins by frequency decile values and undermines the intended separation from raw frequency.
findings.reproduction: Use 20 active items, all with counts[item]=1 and u[item]=1, but vary per-user repetition patterns. The stable argsort assigns the first ten items to decile 0 and the rest to decile 1 despite every item's frequency being identical; each half then gets independently ranked r and p bins.
findings.correction: Fit decile cut points from training-item frequency quantiles and apply the same cut points to equal-frequency items (document and handle duplicate cut points explicitly), rather than assigning ranks that split ties. Keep all fitting restricted to training items.
